question: How large is a pure-measurement 'speedup' when the candidate and the reference are the SAME binary?

protocol.design: arms A and B are the identical jackhmmer binary; a nonzero A/B ratio is therefore pure measurement noise
protocol.backend: Slurm, one node, one job, arms alternate inside the job
protocol.note: run on UniRef90; query set is the 25-query Full subset

gate_statistic.definition: median over R adjacent A/B pair ratios (the statistic the acceptance threshold is compared against)
gate_statistic.note: R=6 is degenerate (only one distinct subset); treat R>=4 as extrapolated

pooled_pair_ratios.definition: resampled pairs drawn ACROSS passes, so each ratio carries between-pass drift; describes a gate that does not cancel drift

recommendation_from_source_report.min_pairs_definition: smallest R with 4.0 x sigma(median over R WITHIN-REPLICATE pairs) < the OLD threshold 0.1
recommendation_from_source_report.threshold_definition: max(4.0 x sigma=0.068152, empirical |median| p99=0.032562) at R=2
recommendation_from_source_report.per_query_cap_definition: 99.9th percentile of within-query (slowest / fastest) repeatability, over queries above the floor
recommendation_from_source_report.pairing: within-replicate adjacent A/B (one pair per replicate)
recommendation_from_source_report.design_note: the harness alternates the two arms inside one replicate, so one replicate IS one adjacent pair; this is the statistic the acceptance gate computes

recomputation.authority: results/ and this file were recomputed from zero_effect_raw.jsonl; the values agree with the stored report to 3 decimal places
